title: Surveillance and activation
objective: Explain how resting microglia survey tissue and what 'activation' means.

steps.title: 'Resting' is a misnomer
steps.body:
Two-photon imaging in living brain (2005) showed that so-called resting microglia are anything but: they constantly extend and retract fine processes, sampling their surroundings.

A better word is **surveilling**. Each microglion patrols its own territory, checking for trouble.

steps.title: Activation changes shape and behavior
steps.body:
When microglia detect damage or danger signals (via PRRs like TLRs, B1-L2), they **activate**: they retract their fine processes, take on a more amoeboid shape, move toward the problem, and release cytokines.

Activation isn't a single switch, though; microglia adopt many states depending on the signal.

flag.note: The old 'M1/M2' two-state model of microglial activation is now considered too simple; microglia show a spectrum of states.

steps.prompt: What did live two-photon imaging reveal about 'resting' microglia?
options: That resting microglia never move at all under normal conditions
That their processes constantly move and sample the surrounding tissue
That microglia are really neurons that have been mislabeled
That microglia appear in the brain only after an injury occurs
steps.explanation: Constant process motility redefined resting microglia as active surveillants, a landmark use of in vivo imaging (a technique revisited in C9/C11).

steps.setup: You injure a tiny spot in the cortex and watch nearby microglia live.
steps.prompt: What do you expect their processes to do?
options: Retract away from the injury and leave the area undefended
Rapidly extend toward the injury site to wall it off
Freeze completely in place and stop moving altogether
Transform into new neurons to replace the damaged tissue
steps.reveal: Microglial processes rapidly converge on a local injury, walling it off and responding, one of the first behaviors seen with in vivo imaging.

steps.prompt: Why has the 'M1 vs M2' label for microglia fallen out of favor?
options: Because microglia turn out not to activate under any condition
Because real microglia show a spectrum of states, not just two
Because there are actually exactly three defined microglial states
Because the M1 and M2 terms were in truth never used by anyone
steps.explanation: Transcriptomic work shows many context-dependent states, so a clean two-category model oversimplifies, a caution worth carrying into any 'activated vs resting' claim.
